Cartesian coordinates across the whole genome

Source: R/coord-locus.R
coord_genome.Rd

Places whole chromosomes end to end on one linear x-axis, for genome-wide tracks such as copy number. Works like coord_loci() with every chromosome as a window: the x-axis is labeled with chromosome names, and alternate chromosomes are shaded.

Usage

coord_genome(
  chromosomes = c(1:22, "X", "Y"),
  seqlengths = NULL,
  gap = 0,
  dividers = TRUE,
  shade = "gray95",
  expand = FALSE,
  clip = "on"
)

Arguments

chromosomes

Chromosomes to show, in order, with or without the chr prefix. Default: 1-22, X, and Y.

seqlengths

Named vector of chromosome lengths, default: hg38 from BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.

gap

Space between chromosomes as a fraction of the total axis, default: 0

dividers

Draw dashed lines between chromosomes, default: TRUE

shade

Fill color of every other chromosome, default: "gray95". Use NA for none.

expand

If TRUE, the default, adds a small expansion to the window limits.

clip

Should drawing be clipped to the extent of the plot panel? Default: "on"

Value

List of a coord and an x-axis scale, added to a plot with +

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ggplot2::ggplot(cn_segments) +
  geom_bed_track(ggplot2::aes(y = sample, fill = cn)) +
  coord_genome() +
  theme_genomic()
} # }
